title: Plano's Tyler Technologies picks up big-name clients like NASA, Justice Department with latest acquisition
summary: Tyler Technologies announced its acquisition of MicroPact for approximately $185 million, adding major federal clients like NASA and the Department of Justice to its roster. This acquisition significantly expands Tyler Technologies' presence in the federal government sector, which previously constituted less than 1% of its business. The deal also brings new software products and insights from MicroPact's partner-driven business model to Tyler Technologies.

title: WeWork signs a deal for 11 floors in State Street’s longtime home
summary: WeWork has signed its largest Boston lease yet, taking 11 floors at One Lincoln Street, formerly State Street Corp.'s long-time home. This expansion will add 4,000 desks and bring WeWork's total Boston-area footprint to 1.1 million square feet, making it a major player in the local office market. However, questions remain about the sustainability of its rapid growth, especially given its reported losses and the potential impact of a future recession.

title: Amazon reports record-breaking holiday sales and earnings, but investors aren’t impressed
summary: Amazon reported record-breaking holiday sales and earnings for its fourth quarter, exceeding analyst expectations with $3 billion in profit and $72.4 billion in revenue. Despite these strong results, the company's stock declined due to a forecast of slowing growth and anticipated increased spending amid HQ2 expansion. This marks the second consecutive holiday quarter Amazon beat estimates, a feat not achieved since 2009.

title: Starbucks executive Rosalind Brewer joins Amazon board (Video)
summary: Rosalind Brewer, a Starbucks executive and 2018 PSBJ Women of Influence honoree, has joined Amazon's board. This appointment follows past criticism of Amazon, including from shareholder Rev. Jesse Jackson, regarding the lack of diversity on its executive team and board.

title: Amazon’s Long Island City HQ will send Altice USA packing
summary: Amazon's planned takeover of Savanna's One Court Square in Long Island City is forcing broadband giant Altice USA to relocate. Altice USA will move from One Court Square to The Paragon, a nearby converted warehouse, filling its entire 130,000 square feet. This move highlights the immediate impact of Amazon's presence on the Long Island City office and residential markets.

title: Amazon names Starbucks executive Rosalind Brewer to its board
summary: Amazon.com Inc. has appointed Rosalind Brewer, Starbucks Corp's Chief Operating Officer, to its board of directors, making her the first black director of the e-commerce giant. This appointment follows Amazon's commitment last year to increase diversity on its board. Brewer also joins Amazon's leadership development and compensation committee.

title: Could a proposed casino revive the York Galleria Mall?
summary: A proposed mini-casino by Penn National at the York Galleria Mall's former Sears site is hoped to revive the struggling mall, which has lost $30 million in assessed value over 20 years. The casino is expected to draw new interest, potentially attracting other businesses and generating up to $1 million annually for Springettsbury Township. This development aligns with a broader trend of malls redefining their roles as mixed-use hubs beyond traditional retail, adapting to societal changes and online shopping.

title: Grocery Wholesaler UNFI Reorganizes Pacific Northwest Distribution Network
summary: UNFI (United Natural Foods Inc.) is reorganizing its Pacific Northwest distribution network to improve synergies following its acquisition of Supervalu. The company plans to build a new 1.2 million-square-foot facility in Centralia, Wash., and expand a current Ridgefield, Wash., facility to 800,000 square feet, which will lead to the closure of three existing distribution centers. This optimization aims to enhance inventory management, logistics, and achieve synergy goals related to the Supervalu acquisition.

title: Amazon Eases Into Self-Driving Tech By Joining Aurora's $530 Million Funding Surge
summary: Aurora, a self-driving technology startup founded by leading researchers, secured over $530 million in Series B funding, with Amazon making a significant investment. The company aims to develop autonomous vehicle technology for other manufacturers rather than building its own fleet. This substantial funding injection underscores the capital-intensive nature of autonomous driving development and Amazon's interest in logistics and goods movement.

title: Scientists’ discovery could mean less-expensive smartphones, TVs
summary: USC chemists have developed a new copper-based compound that could replace rare and expensive iridium in smartphone and TV screens, potentially leading to cheaper devices without compromising visual quality. This discovery addresses the scarcity of iridium and solves the long-standing problem of short lifetimes for blue light emission in OLED technology. The new rigid copper compound exhibits efficient light emission comparable to iridium, opening new possibilities for display technology and energy-efficient lighting.

title: A Storm Is Coming to the Global Music Industry — and More than $100 Billion Is at Stake
summary: Vivendi is selling up to 50% of Universal Music Group, and its projected astronomical valuation could significantly impact the valuations of rivals Sony Music and Warner Music Group. Analysts from Deutsche Bank, Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs, and Exane BNP Paribas have provided valuations for UMG ranging from $29 billion to $42 billion, with a "bull case" scenario for Morgan Stanley suggesting even higher figures based on streaming growth. This potential Universal Music Group supersale could lead to a combined valuation for the "big three" music companies exceeding $100 billion, driven by intense market demand and optimistic streaming forecasts.

title: Opinion: Amazon should buy Netflix — and 9 other mergers we’d love to see
summary: Despite rising interest rates and market volatility, 2019 is expected to continue the trend of large-scale mergers and acquisitions, following five consecutive years of M&A activity exceeding $3 trillion. The article suggests several potential "mega-deals" that could occur, highlighting that corporate America remains undeterred in pursuing significant transactions. Examples given from 2018 include Cigna Corp.'s $54 billion purchase of Express Scripts and the pending $26 billion merger between Sprint Corp. and T-Mobile US.

title: Ryder System opens facilities due to e-commerce offering
summary: Ryder System has launched a new e-commerce fulfillment offering for manufacturers that conduct business online. This initiative includes opening two new multi-client facilities in California and Texas and expanding an existing warehouse in Pennsylvania, all expected to be fully operational by May. The service provides an alternative to third-party marketplaces, facilitating direct-to-consumer order fulfillment and demonstrating significant volume growth and shipping accuracy.

title: Google selects Equinix for submarine cable landing station in LA
summary: Google has chosen Equinix's LA4 data center as the landing point for its upcoming Curie submarine cable, which will connect the US with Chile. This marks the first direct submarine link between the two countries in 20 years. The cable, named after Marie Skłodowska Curie, will stretch over 10,000 km and aims to meet the increasing demand for high-capacity, low-latency global connectivity.

title: Ryder drives into Amazon Marketplace turf
summary: Ryder System Inc. is launching an e-commerce fulfillment solution to compete with platforms like Amazon, offering manufacturers direct control over their product fulfillment. The solution includes new multi-client facilities in California and Texas, and an expanded one in Pennsylvania, all slated to be operational by May. Ryder's initiative aims to provide manufacturers with greater control over inventory, pricing, and customer service while maintaining speed to market.

title: Alphabet Dethrones Amazon As Top U.S. Internet Company: Citi Report
summary: Citigroup has re-ranked Alphabet as the top U.S. internet company, surpassing Amazon, due to its strong growth in mobile search and YouTube, stock buybacks, and high valuation. Amazon's downgrade to fourth place is attributed to slower growth, regulatory challenges in India, and distractions from its HQ2 plans and CEO's personal issues. This re-ranking coincides with Google Cloud's aggressive investment in its sales division and increased competition with Amazon Web Services and Microsoft Azure.

title: FedEx Names Raj Subramaniam New President, COO
summary: FedEx Corp. has named Raj Subramaniam as its new president and chief operating officer, succeeding David Bronczek who is retiring. Subramaniam, who previously served as president and CEO of FedEx Express, will also become co-president and co-CEO of FedEx Services. His new role will commence on March 1, 2019, according to FedEx.

title: Walmart on a roll
summary: Walmart is experiencing strong growth, marked by a $1.7 million remodeling project at its Pueblo superstore and impressive holiday sales nationwide. The company reported its strongest holiday quarter in years, with a 4.2% jump in same-store sales and a 43% increase in e-commerce sales, signaling its growing competitiveness against online giants like Amazon. Walmart's success is attributed to a robust economy, strategic investments in store upgrades and employee wages, and an expanding online presence.

title: Walmart flexes in the fourth quarter, beats all expectations
summary: Walmart significantly exceeded Wall Street's expectations for its fiscal fourth quarter profits and sales, driven by strong e-commerce growth and robust performance across various product categories. This positive report defied a gloomy December government retail sales report, indicating that Walmart's strategic investments in online services and grocery pickup are widening its competitive advantage. The company's strong results suggest that consumers are benefiting from a stronger economy, enabling Walmart to attract a broader demographic and pose a more serious threat to Amazon in the online retail space.

title: Amazon.com, Inc. | Case Study
summary: This case study from MIT Sloan examines Amazon.com, Inc.'s financial strategy and growth over its first 20 years since its IPO. It highlights Amazon's focus on investing in expansion and R&D at the expense of short-term accounting earnings, aiming for long-term value creation. The study also discusses Amazon's use of cash flow performance measures in its non-GAAP disclosures and asks students to consider pathways to higher profitability.

title: Tilray to acquire Manitoba Harvest
summary: Tilray has acquired FHF Holdings, the parent company of hemp-based food company Manitoba Harvest, from Compass Group Diversified Holdings. This acquisition expands Tilray's product portfolio into natural foods and provides access to Manitoba Harvest's manufacturing facilities and retail network. Manitoba Harvest plans to launch CBD products this summer in legal US markets and later in Canada once edibles are legal, leveraging Tilray's expertise with cannabinoids.

title: Amazon.com 'Insourcing' Roils Freight Industry, Analysts Say
summary: Amazon's increasing "insourcing" of its freight operations is causing significant disruption in the trucking and logistics industry, leading to the bankruptcy of New England Motor Freight and a substantial revenue loss for XPO Logistics. Industry analysts and former Amazon employees suggest that Amazon aims to become a dominant third-party logistics (3PL) provider by handling more of its shipping needs internally. This strategy forces other carriers to re-evaluate their business models and prepares them for intensified competition.

title: Kemp 360 Vision analyzes F5, Nginx data
summary: Kemp Technologies has updated its 360 Vision predictive analytics service to include data from F5 Networks and Nginx load balancers, allowing for multivendor ADC ecosystem management. This SaaS application identifies potential problems and suggests remediation steps, with upcoming support for KVM, AWS, and Microsoft Azure. The update also adds automated load balancer deployment to Kemp 360 Central.

title: Former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi Joins Amazon’s Board
summary: Former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi has been elected to Amazon.com Inc.'s board of directors, joining its audit committee. Her appointment brings Amazon's board to 11 members, continuing a refresh of the panel. This marks the second new board appointee for Amazon this month.

title: Amazon adds former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi to board
summary: Amazon.com Inc has appointed former PepsiCo Inc CEO Indra Nooyi to its board of directors, making her the second woman added to the board this month. Nooyi's appointment increases the number of women on Amazon's eleven-member board to five, aligning with the company's new policy to increase diversity. She will be part of the audit committee and has been granted 549 shares of common stock.

title: Indra Nooyi, former CEO of Pepsico, appointed to Amazon's board of directors
summary: Former PepsiCo CEO Indra Nooyi was appointed to Amazon's board of directors and its audit committee on February 25, 2019. This appointment follows her extensive career at PepsiCo, where she served as CEO and chairman. In connection with her election, Ms. Nooyi received a restricted stock unit award of 549 shares of Amazon common stock.

title: Target rips a page from Walmart, Amazon, welcoming outside sellers to website
summary: Target is launching Target+, an invite-only marketplace that will allow third-party sellers to offer a curated selection of products on its website, similar to Walmart and Amazon. This move aims to expand Target's online assortment while maintaining quality control by selectively inviting sellers. Shoppers using Target+ can still benefit from Red Card discounts, free shipping, and in-store returns for purchased items.

title: Target taking aim at Victoria's Secret with new lingerie brands
summary: Target is launching three new lingerie brands—Auden, Colsie, and Stars Above—to compete in the $12 billion lingerie market. This move directly targets Victoria's Secret by offering a more inclusive approach with diverse sizing and body-positive marketing, replacing its older Gilligan & O'Malley line. The new lines emphasize comfort and cater to a broad demographic, with all bras priced under $22.

title: The Value Chain Constraint
summary: This article analyzes how companies like Amazon, Walmart, Google, and Microsoft succeed or struggle based on their integration within specific value chains, rather than solely on technological innovation. It argues that sustainable differentiation comes from effectively integrating different component pieces of a value chain, and that straying too far from this core integration can lead even large tech companies to struggle in new markets despite massive resources. The author uses examples like Amazon's grocery struggles, Google Cloud's challenges, and Microsoft's enterprise success to illustrate the concept, and Netflix's transformation as an exception that proves the rule.

title: Icee to bring 200-plus jobs, headquarters to La Vergne
summary: Icee, the national frozen beverage company, is moving its corporate headquarters from California to La Vergne, Tennessee, creating over 200 new jobs with an average annual pay of $60,152. This $10.3 million investment includes a new 85,000-square-foot office and distribution center, supported by a seven-year property tax break valued at $690,275 from the Rutherford County Industrial Development Board. The company's decision was influenced by La Vergne's central location, business-friendly environment, and strong workforce development.

title: How Netflix created a $1 billion arms race for TV writers
summary: Netflix has instigated a highly competitive environment for TV writers and showrunners, signing major deals worth hundreds of millions of dollars with creators like Shonda Rhimes, Ryan Murphy, and Kenya Barris. This "arms race" is driven by streaming companies building original content libraries and traditional studios consolidating, leading to immense value placed on showrunners who can create intellectual property. The article explores the motivations behind these mega-deals, their structure (often including upfront payments in lieu of residuals), and the implications for both creators and the broader entertainment industry.

title: Etsy to offset carbon emissions from shipping its products
summary: Etsy announced its plan to offset carbon emissions from shipping products sold on its platform, starting with covering all U.S. e-commerce shipping emissions for one day. The company will purchase carbon offsets for ongoing shipping, focusing on projects like wind power and forest protection. This initiative aims to address the 98% of Etsy's total emissions that come from product shipping, despite Etsy not actively managing the shipping process itself.

title: JBG Smith reveals details on executive pay, Amazon bonuses
summary: JBG Smith CEO Matt Kelly received $11.3 million in total compensation in 2018, including a significant equity award of $6.6 billion. This substantial bonus was awarded for his pivotal role in securing Amazon.com Inc.'s second headquarters in Northern Virginia. The article also mentions that winning Amazon's HQ2 meant big bonuses for executives.

title: Alicia Boler-Davis Out, Gerald Johnson In As General Motors Exec VP Of Global Manufacturing
summary: General Motors has appointed Gerald Johnson as the new Executive Vice President of Global Manufacturing, effective April 1. Johnson replaces Alicia Boler-Davis, who is leaving the company to pursue other opportunities after 25 years of service. Mary Barra, GM Chairman and CEO, highlighted Johnson's strong leadership and experience as integral to the company's transformation and future mobility efforts.
